sentences.text: Baurutitan was estimated to be 12 to 14 meters long and about 3.5 meters tall.
This large long-necked herbivorous sauropod was also estimated to be between 12 and 16 meters long.
It was the fourth sauropod described in Brazil, following Antarctosaurus, Gondwanatitan, and Amazonsaurus.
The type species Baurutitan britoi was officially described in 2005 by Kellner and colleagues, even though the fossils were discovered in 1957.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was found in 1957 by the Brazilian paleontologist Llewellyn Ivor Price in the Peirópolis region of Minas Gerais.
Price conducted excavations at an old quarry known as Quarry Caieira on the São Luis farm.
Excavations at Quarry Caieira recovered fossils of turtles, crocodylomorphs, theropods, sauropods, fish, freshwater invertebrates, trace fossils, egg fragments, and plant debris.
The holotype consists of a series of 19 vertebrae, including the last sacral and 18 caudals, which were initially named 'Series C' before becoming the holotype of Baurutitan.
All recovered fossil material is stored in the collection of the Earth Science Museum in Rio de Janeiro.
The name Baurutitan combines 'bauru', referring to the geographical region, and 'titan' from Greek myths, while 'britoi' honors Brazilian paleontologist Ignacio Aureliano Brito Machado.
Baurutitan fossils were found in the Serra da Galga Formation near Uberaba in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais.
The holotype specimen was found in the Marilia Formation, dating to the Maastrichtian epoch, about 72 to 66 million years ago.
Baurutitan lived during the Maastrichtian epoch, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
